nonLabourLines.description: Legacy data migration tooling / Oracle connectors / cloud migration compute
Staging environment cloud infra (CI/CD, hosting) setup and first month
Contingency / misc licensing (design tools, PDF generation library)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; all estimates are derived from backlog point sizing and standard delivery ratios, not past performance on this project.
1 story point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended engineering effort, adjusted per task based on described complexity (e.g. migration and payment integration weighted heavier due to risk).

Backend Developer is staffed at 1.5 FTE (~240 hrs/mo capacity) but the backlog requires ~620 hours of backend work concentrated in RBAC, payments, dashboard, and migration; this role is the primary bottleneck and may need timeline extension or temporary contractor support to hit an aggressive schedule.

Frontend Developer is a single 1.0 FTE resource (~160 hrs/mo); 420 hours implies roughly 2.5 months of dedicated frontend effort across the design system, dashboard, invoice UI, and RBAC UI enforcement.
QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE (~96 hrs/mo) is allocated 220 hours, concentrated on the higher-risk Urgent items (auth, payments) and migration validation; lower-priority items get lighter QA pass.

DevOps Engineer at 0.4 FTE (~64 hrs/mo) covers CI/CD setup and ongoing pipeline/staging support; migration infra work is scoped mostly as non-labour cloud/tooling spend rather than additional DevOps hours given limited capacity.

PW-8 (Legacy data migration, 21 points) is treated as the highest-effort, highest-risk item; its complexity (400k customer records, 2M invoice lines from Oracle) is assumed to require significant backend scripting/validation effort plus dedicated migration tooling spend.
Non-labour costs cover Stripe/PCI review, migration tooling and cloud compute, staging infra setup, and minor licensing/tooling contingency.

Best case assumes no significant rework, migration proceeds cleanly, and RBAC/permission matrix is simpler than described. Worst case assumes migration data-quality issues, additional Stripe reconciliation edge cases, and RBAC UI/API rework.
Estimate excludes ongoing post-launch support/maintenance costs, which would be a separate phase.
input.reasoning: Effort was sized bottom-up per backlog item using story points as a proxy for complexity, translated into role-specific hours based on the nature of each task (backend-heavy for auth/RBAC/payments/migration, frontend-heavy for design system/dashboard/invoice UI, QA weighted toward Urgent-priority and migration validation, DevOps concentrated on the CI/staging setup task). Total labour hours were then checked against each role's stated FTE availability to flag capacity risk — Backend Developer in particular is asked to absorb more hours than its 1.5 FTE would comfortably deliver within a short timeframe, which is called out as an assumption/risk rather than silently padded or reallocated to an unstaffed role. Non-labour costs were added for the concrete infra/tooling needs implied by the backlog (Stripe/PCI, migration tooling, staging cloud infra, misc licensing). The most-likely scenario equals the sum of all line items; best/worst case scenarios were derived by flexing the highest-risk items (migration, payments, RBAC) down or up roughly 10-15% to reflect schedule/complexity uncertainty, consistent with the absence of historical actuals.

reductions.description: Descope PW-2 (Design system and component library) to a minimal set (buttons, forms, tables only) and defer theming tokens/dialogs to a later phase
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend Developer hours by ~50 hours; ships a functional but less polished component library now, with full design system completed post-launch.

reductions.description: Reduce QA hours on Medium-priority items (PW-2, PW-6) by relying more on developer self-testing and automated test coverage instead of dedicated QA passes
reductions.effect: Cuts ~40 QA Engineer hours; slightly increases regression risk on lower-priority features, mitigated by CI pipeline test gates from PW-1.

reductions.description: Defer PW-8 (Legacy data migration) scope to migrate only active/recent customer records and invoices in this phase, with historical archive migrated in a later phase
reductions.effect: Reduces backend hours and migration tooling/compute spend significantly by shrinking the data volume handled in this phase; full historical migration becomes a follow-on project.

reductions.description: Delay DevOps-managed staging environment cloud spend by using a lighter-weight shared staging setup instead of a dedicated environment in month one
reductions.effect: Reduces non-labour infra cost for PW-1; slight increase in environment contention risk during initial development.
